title: Rank-Constrained Adaptation for Reliable Real-World Performance
claim: A standard classifier misclassifies a minority subgroup; a low-rank correction along error-concentrated directions fixes it without full retraining.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, ERM boundary, error-covariance eigenspectrum, then corrected boundary
description: Three boxed panels run left to right with a dotted legend below. The left panel shows a 2-D toy dataset split by a horizontal line labeled W0. Orange squares (class 0) and green squares (class 1) are the majority groups. Orange circles and green circles are a minority group and sit inside pink blobs marking the misclassified region. The middle panel shows the error covariance formula C = sum e_i x_i x_i^T. Under it is a bar chart of decreasing eigenvalues λ1 to λ4 in graded red tones, labeled top-k eigenspace and U_k, and below that the update W = W0 + U_k a. The right panel shows the same points with a tilted diagonal line labeled W that separates all the points correctly, with no pink blobs. The legend maps color to class and shape to group.
caption: \textbf{\methodname{}.} (Left) ERM can learn a decision boundary that performs well on average while systematically misclassifying a subpopulation. (Middle) \methodname{} assigns larger weights to examples where the model gives low probability to the true label, and uses these weights to identify important directions in representation space. (Right) \methodname{} learns a rank-restricted additive correction to the classifier logits along these directions, improving classification for affected samples without unrestricted classifier retraining. Colors denote class labels, while marker shapes denote attribute groups.
abstract: Deep learning models trained to optimize average accuracy often exhibit systematic failures on particular subpopulations. In real-world settings like healthcare, the subpopulations most affected by such disparities are frequently unlabeled, partially observed, or not known in advance. Existing group-robust methods typically assume prior knowledge of the relevant subgroups, using group annotations for training, validation, or model selection. We propose Misclassification Aware Rank-Limited Adaptation (MARLA), a parameter-efficient method for improving worst group performance without explicit subgroup annotations. MARLA leverages an ERM-trained model by calculating the model's misclassification probability scores on a held-out adaptation set to identify a low-dimensional subspace where errors concentrate. We then learn a rank-restricted additive correction to the classifier logits within that subspace. Across seven real-world datasets, we evaluate group robustness under three settings: no knowledge of subgroup relevance, partial knowledge of subgroup relevance, and full knowledge of subgroup relevance. MARLA improves worst-group performance while remaining fast and parameter-efficient, with data-guided hyperparameter selection.
